meaning: Implemented within the stated profile; not universal standards or platform conformance.

items.title: Typed property metadata and support contract
items.research_acceptance: Every accepted property has a consumer, stated fallback or rejection; a paint-only token change does not trigger layout.
profiles: Compile-time metadata, typed authoring, validation, initial values, interpolation and invalidation for 37 native box/text properties plus a separately reflected native Paragraph catalog. Computed values feed existing Frame/Tree/Texts and Stack consumers.
verification: direct typed values reach existing box and text consumers; transparent and zero are values
paint-only changes do not request shaping or layout; text metrics do
caller usage: resolved paragraph tokens drive the real shaping and multiline layout path
limitations: Advanced brushes, effects and layout side tables retain their own typed inputs rather than becoming unused Style fields.
Backend resource/material support remains the renderer's capability contract; the style catalog does not manufacture a missing backend feature.

items.title: Caller-owned optional style storage
items.research_acceptance: Exhausting a declared pool returns a deterministic failure without allocation, corruption or silently missing properties.
profiles: Direct borrowed slices remain sufficient; optional caller-owned declaration pools return deterministic capacity errors and generation-checked spans. Compiler, provenance and token-scale output use declared destination buffers.
verification: bounded authoring storage rejects overflow and stale spans without losing current declarations
cycles and scale capacity errors are explicit
compiler errors report unsupported input and bounded storage without ignoring declarations
limitations: The caller keeps borrowed data alive and owns mutation/revision sequencing.
Store generations wrap modulo u64 while skipping zero; spans must not survive a complete epoch wrap or replacement of their owning store.

items.title: Explicit presence and inheritance
items.research_acceptance: A transparent literal stays transparent under a colored parent; inherit follows the parent; an explicit override stops propagation.
profiles: Tagged literal/inherit/initial/token sources with omission as absence, selected inherited text/cursor properties, and independent paragraph inheritance. Explicit transparent, null and numeric zero survive resolution.
verification: explicit inheritance, initial, zero and transparent remain distinct, also at comptime
paragraph presence and invalidation distinguish inherited, initial, null and zero
limitations: Existing theme.Inherited sentinel-based APIs remain available for compatibility; callers opt into the explicit declaration resolver.

items.title: Role-preserving semantic color tokens
items.research_acceptance: Two roles can share the same original RGBA value and diverge on theme change while an equal literal remains unchanged.
profiles: Named typed tokens, lexical aliases, nearest-scope lookup and final-origin records preserve role identity independently of packed RGBA equality; application-defined roles need no registry.
verification: caller usage: same-value semantic tokens separate on a theme change, literals stay literal
same-valued roles keep their identities; a child scope and lexical alias differ
DTCG generated semantic aliases and typography feed actual text layout
limitations: Applications choose their semantic vocabulary; stock convenience defaults are a deliberately small palette, not every domain role.

items.title: Spacing, typography and shape token scales
items.research_acceptance: Changing density updates dependent spacing and hit targets without accidentally scaling physical strokes or fixed assets.
profiles: Caller-authored monotone numeric scales, bridges for existing spacing/radius/type scales, explicit density and text scaling, and generated composite typography/border/elevation values with native consumers.
verification: cycles and scale capacity errors are explicit
default recipe respects environment text scale and keeps focus separate from selected border
DTCG generated semantic aliases and typography feed actual text layout
DTCG generated gradients, shadows and borders paint caller-owned pixels
limitations: Density changes only the tokens chosen by the caller; separate hit-target policies are not silently scaled.
Generated typography selects a supplied static font catalog entry; variable-font instance creation remains explicit.

items.title: Scoped themes and deterministic precedence
items.research_acceptance: A nested theme changes its descendants only; the inspector can identify the winning source for conflicting values.
profiles: Component base, inherited values, ordered matched declarations and local property overrides lower deterministically; explicit nested token scopes and final optional system-color policy report their winning provenance.
verification: same-valued roles keep their identities; a child scope and lexical alias differ
caller usage: simultaneous states, orthogonal variants and local transparent overrides
inspector explains a real compiled rule winner, inactive state and local override
system colors override authored paint with provenance and explicit component exceptions
limitations: This is ordered native merging, not CSS origin/specificity/cascade-layer semantics.
The caller associates tree subtrees with scope indices; no retained theme manager walks the application automatically.

items.title: Reusable widget part styles
items.research_acceptance: A shared thumb recipe styles slider and range handles without changing their value or input semantics.
profiles: Stable common part IDs plus arbitrary application IDs; independent label/icon/mark/track/thumb/fill/focus resolution reaches real controls. Slider and range recipes share the same thumb property vocabulary while retaining their native value semantics.
verification: recipe caller: custom thumb and app-defined part use direct data, no registry
caller usage: custom icon/label retains button activation and disabled prevents it
radio and range recipes preserve keyboard and pointer behavior with shared marks and two visible thumbs
limitations: A decorative part is allocated as a node only by a builder that needs one; a recipe ID alone does not allocate a tree row.
Range knobs use validated explicit pixel dimensions in the supplied adapter.

items.title: Named variants and reusable component recipes
items.research_acceptance: Combining a small destructive button variant with a local text-color override preserves the remaining recipe values.
profiles: Borrowed recipes and variant-ID slices compose intent, size, density and application variants per property, with component-local values applied last before any explicit system-color policy.
verification: caller usage: simultaneous states, orthogonal variants and local transparent overrides
caller usage: combined states keep independent border/focus and failed resolution leaves frame balanced
limitations: Variant names have application-defined meanings; there is no global registration or implicit inheritance of variant membership.

items.title: Combinable state-dependent styling
items.research_acceptance: Selected plus hovered plus keyboard-focused retains selection and visible focus; disabled behavior cannot be enabled by a paint override.
profiles: Required/forbidden masks cover built-in interaction/semantic states plus caller custom bits; ordered declarations preserve independent selection and keyboard focus without enumerating every state combination.
verification: caller usage: simultaneous states, orthogonal variants and local transparent overrides
recipe disabled state cancels capture, skips Tab and cannot be defeated by a visual override
recipe read-only checkbox remains focusable and its pointer event is explicitly suppressed
combined state and environment row participation cancels captured range and radio actions in both front ends
limitations: Focus-within, dragging, drop-target and domain states are supplied by the owner when not directly produced by the standard adapter.
Style resolution does not itself mutate application behavior or semantic truth.

items.title: Shared style handles and targeted invalidation
items.research_acceptance: Hovering one control in a large list recomputes its affected style values without re-resolving unrelated rows.
profiles: Optional bounded cache stores reached combinations using exact state/environment keys and caller-owned recipe/token/parent revisions. Metadata and differences expose the concrete dirty domains for independently scheduled passes.
verification: optional cache agrees with direct resolution and generation changes invalidate a reached state
paint-only changes do not request shaping or layout; text metrics do
inspector explains a real compiled rule winner, inactive state and local override
limitations: Base/declaration/local/variant changes must advance the recipe revision; mutable borrowed data is not observed automatically.
No mandatory interning, subscription graph or global invalidation traversal exists; the host schedules affected requests and clears before revision reuse/wrap.

items.title: Unified runtime and compile-time authoring
items.research_acceptance: One styled control produces equivalent supported draw output in runtime and compile-time paths with explicit unsupported diagnostics.
profiles: Same typed resolver at runtime and comptime, direct computed values, optional diagonal component adapters, dynamic state/environment/token fields and independently callable native passes; production DrawLists and semantic role/value columns are compared by replay consumers.
verification: explicit inheritance, initial, zero and transparent remain distinct, also at comptime
recipe controls: runtime/comptime draw and behavior parity through click, drag, text and theme changes
data part composition has runtime/comptime parity with dynamic state and environment
radio and range recipes preserve keyboard and pointer behavior with shared marks and two visible thumbs
a runtime token error in a comptime recipe is returned as frame data
limitations: Capacity, resource and renderer support remain explicit; parity claims apply to the named supported consumer fixtures rather than all possible arbitrary shaders or widget extensions.

items.title: Optional design-token interchange
items.research_acceptance: Alias cycles and type mismatches fail during import; generated tokens preserve role identity and deterministic output.
profiles: Offline bounded DTCG 2025.10 compiler covers all 13 token categories, inherited group types, aliases and local component references, deterministic native Zig constants and source-preserving metadata. Cycles, missing references, duplicate keys, invalid types/values and capacity limits fail explicitly.
verification: python3 tools/stylegen/test_stylegen.py
DTCG generated semantic aliases and typography feed actual text layout
DTCG generated gradients, shadows and borders paint caller-owned pixels
DTCG generated transition timing and custom stroke use native playback and stroking
limitations: Declared profile rejects group $extends, remote references, missing color components and unsupported unit expressions.
rem conversion, seconds and radius-to-sigma lowering are explicit target settings; existing RGBA8 packing clamps color at its boundary.
DTCG is a Community Group specification, not a W3C Recommendation.

items.title: Optional CSS-like authoring compiler
items.research_acceptance: Unsupported syntax is diagnosed; accepted rules compile deterministically and never scan source strings during rendering.
profiles: Optional bounded compiler for part/variant/state compounds, comma groups, :not(:state), comments, native property aliases and padding shorthand; output is ordinary Rule/Declaration data with source positions and no render-time source parsing.
verification: compiler caller resolves parsed parts, variants, combined states and explicit transparency
compiler errors report unsupported input and bounded storage without ignoring declarations
compiled declarations feed the actual frame text and layout consumer
limitations: Full CSS selectors, descendant combinators, specificity, @rules/imports/cascade layers, !important, URLs and custom-property definitions are explicitly unsupported.
Output buffers are unspecified on a failed compilation; no partial successful sheet is returned.

items.title: Computed-style and dependency inspector
items.research_acceptance: A conflicting state/variant override can be explained to the exact source and invalidation reason without changing program behavior.
profiles: Caller-owned computed-property snapshots, all rule match reasons, declaration dispositions, literal/inherit/token provenance and concrete invalidation differences; final system policy can supply its own winning origin trace.
verification: inspector explains a real compiled rule winner, inactive state and local override
system colors override authored paint with provenance and explicit component exceptions
limitations: This is read-only inspector data, not a retained inspector UI or an automatic backend capability detector.
inspector.snapshot evaluates raw requests; request Recipe.resolve provenance separately for the recipe's later system-color policy.

items.title: Preferred, minimum and maximum dimensions
items.research_acceptance: Conflicting min/max and aspect ratio produce documented deterministic sizes; percentage values are not incorrectly advertised as new.
profiles: Retains native fit/pixel/grow/percentage/min/max/aspect rows. The optional measured flex pass adds explicit basis and full bounded min/max freezing, then lowers placements to ordinary Style.
verification: min: a node is never smaller than its min, even with no content
percent: a fraction of the parent's inner size on both axes
aspect: the height follows the resolved width, over content, grow and stretch
bounded flex bases freeze repeatedly and auto margins absorb remaining space
limitations: Native Flex preserves its documented max-wins conflict rule, one shrink round and optional two grow rounds; special.flex is the explicit iterative profile.

items.title: Intrinsic content measurement semantics
items.research_acceptance: A wrapped label and unwrapped label report different meaningful minima, and measured sizes agree with final line layout.
profiles: Measures real shaped min-content and max-content widths, mandatory breaks, tab stops, no-break spaces, ordinary versus anywhere wrapping and explicit hyphen opportunities; fit-content lowers to actual Size.px.
verification: intrinsic widths distinguish unbreakable words anywhere tabs and fit content in real layout
limitations: Input glyph clusters must be in logical monotonic order and coarsened to graphemes; measure before visual bidi reordering.
Language-specific hyphen marker widths require fromOpportunities; the basic UAX14 pass does not guess a hyphen glyph.

items.title: Relative length units and bounded expressions
items.research_acceptance: Changing text scale affects font-relative spacing while device-pixel strokes stay fixed; indefinite percentage bases follow documented behavior.
profiles: Caller-resolved logical/device/percentage/font/root-font/line/viewport/container/physical lengths, safe insets and bounded arithmetic/min/max/clamp expressions lower to real Size values.
verification: relative units and expressions feed real layout without a manager or hidden passes
limitations: Font, viewport, container and safe-area bases are caller inputs; indefinite bases return explicit Indefinite.
This is typed bounded expression evaluation, not a CSS calc() text parser.

items.title: Per-edge padding and margins
items.research_acceptance: Margins influence placement without changing paint content bounds; nested margins never collapse implicitly.
profiles: Retains physical per-edge padding and non-collapsing margin rows; logical mapping is explicit; optional measured flex consumes explicit physical margins and automatic margin slots.
verification: margin: adds to the parent's natural size and to the cursor step; the node sits inside it
bounded flex bases freeze repeatedly and auto margins absorb remaining space
logical edges sizes margins and reversed block flow reach physical box geometry
limitations: Native floating nodes retain their documented margin policy; margins are not CSS block margin collapse.
The existing box-size convention remains the core contract; no global CSS content-box/border-box switch is inferred.

items.title: Independent gaps and line spacing
items.research_acceptance: A wrapping panel can have different item and line spacing, and orientation changes map each gap predictably.
profiles: Grid, measured row/column flow, masonry and document columns accept independent axis/line gaps and emit placements consumed by native nodes or text Lines.
verification: grid: gaps between tracks, spans across gaps, and items aligned in their cells
special layouts lower into ordinary node layout and preserve dependent placement
table spans and page fragments drive the real placement and glyph-line columns
limitations: The legacy native flex-wrap side table retains its single Style.gap input; independent line/main gaps use the explicit measured flow pass.

items.title: Direction-aware logical edges and dimensions
items.research_acceptance: Switching LTR to RTL mirrors logical margins and anchors while explicitly physical left/right values obey documented precedence.
profiles: Maps inline/block dimensions, logical padding/margins/insets and axes for horizontal/vertical/sideways writing and LTR/RTL; an optional mirror pass handles reversed box flow.
verification: logical edges sizes margins and reversed block flow reach physical box geometry
limitations: Logical box mapping does not rotate glyphs; vertical_text is the separate text consumer.
Mirroring requires caller-supplied bounded rows and explicit placement sequencing.

items.title: Flex basis, growth and shrink semantics
items.research_acceptance: Unequal shrink weights respect minimum sizes; native bounded results and any CSS-compatible results are separately documented and tested.
profiles: Keeps the native fast profile and adds a measured single-line flex pass with explicit basis, growth/shrink weights, repeated min/max freezing, margins, auto margins, stretch and baseline placement.
verification: bounded flex bases freeze repeatedly and auto margins absorb remaining space
regrow: bounded to two rounds; a grower capped in the second leaves its rest unused
limitations: The measured pass is explicitly sequenced by the caller and does not replace the native SIMD row profile.
No browser flexbox conformance claim; complex multi-line flex interactions remain explicit composition.

items.title: Wrapping, line layout and baseline alignment
items.research_acceptance: Wrapped rows of mixed font sizes align by the selected baseline without clipping; unsupported profile combinations reject explicitly.
profiles: Retains native row wrap and first-baseline rows; measured flow supports either main axis with independent gaps; explicit baseline values and inline-object metrics align mixed content. Paragraph.baseline_source selects first/last measured text baselines for the ordinary native baseline rows; the explicit metrics commit helper does the same for custom paragraphs.
verification: wrap: when everything fits on one line the rects are those of a row that does not wrap
baseline alignment: children of a baseline row share one baseline
special layouts lower into ordinary node layout and preserve dependent placement
inline replacement participates in wrapping baseline metrics and transformed image emission
edge trim and selected last baselines drive glyph queries and native baseline layout
limitations: Native baseline alignment remains restricted to non-wrapping rows; first/last text baseline selection is implemented, but full automatic multi-line flex baseline-sharing groups are outside that profile.
Reverse flow uses logical mirroring or caller order; there is no separate implicit CSS order cascade.

items.title: Container and item alignment distribution
items.research_acceptance: Space-evenly includes both outer gaps; safe alignment keeps overflowing content reachable instead of centering it offscreen.
profiles: Grid and measured placement support start/end/center/space-between/space-around/space-evenly; native item cross overrides and grid stretch are retained. Negative spare space is clamped in measured distribution.
verification: grid content distribution and bounded fit tracks set cell starts
cross: a child's own alignment replaces the parent's across the main axis
bounded flex bases freeze repeatedly and auto margins absorb remaining space
limitations: Self/baseline semantics are explicit for each layout profile; there is no universal CSS alignment resolver.

items.title: Public integration of bounded grid
items.research_acceptance: A normal frontend can build a spanned grid; out-of-capacity placement preserves the documented overflow flag and never writes outside buffers.
profiles: Public bounded grid rows and run/fit/resolve passes support fixed/content/fraction tracks, explicit cells/spans, independent gaps, item alignment and sparse automatic placement.
verification: grid: items in explicit cells; fit tracks take the largest item, items fill their cell
grid: gaps between tracks, spans across gaps, and items aligned in their cells
autoPlace: row order around explicit items, spans that do not fit move on
limitations: Track/content contributions use the declared native profile rather than the full browser Grid sizing algorithm.

items.title: Richer grid tracks and placement
items.research_acceptance: Automatic track creation respects capacity, named areas resolve deterministically and dense placement never changes semantic focus order implicitly.
profiles: Adds min/max and bounded fit-content tracks, fractional freezing, row/column dense placement, definite-size auto-fill/auto-fit expansion and bounded implicit track patterns. Borrowed named lines with positive/negative occurrences and validated rectangular named areas resolve into real numeric grid items/spans.
verification: bounded grid fractions honor minima caps and redistribution in actual cell geometry
dense and column auto flow use bounded existing cells
automatic repeats and bounded implicit patterns feed actual grid track sizing
named lines and rectangular areas resolve to actual grid node geometry
limitations: Names are resolved explicitly from caller rows/templates; this does not add a CSS selector/tokenizer or an implicit name registry.
auto-fit uses a caller-supplied occupied-track count; intrinsic automatic-repeat browser rules are not inferred.
A distinct min-content floor is supplied explicitly rather than guessed from a maximum-content measurement.

items.title: Subgrid alignment across nested components
items.research_acceptance: Nested form rows align to parent tracks and update after a parent resize without indefinite layout retries.
profiles: An explicit parent-item relation shares row or column track definitions, intrinsic contributions, resolved lines and inherited gap values across nested grids.
verification: shared subgrid contributes individual intrinsic tracks and reuses resolved lines
limitations: Parent grids must precede children, shared counts must match the parent item span, and shared-axis child padding must be zero.
Automatic CSS subgrid baseline participation and arbitrary cyclic dependencies are outside this bounded profile.

items.title: Out-of-flow placement and containing blocks
items.research_acceptance: An absolutely positioned badge is excluded from sibling layout and resolves percentage insets against the documented containing box.
profiles: Floating rows retain an explicit containing parent/origin; ordinary offsets, logical inset resolution and anchor/pivot passes lower to normal geometry.
verification: anchor: corners and edges of the parent's content box, with the subtree carried along
anchor: no anchors leaves the layout untouched; overflow is reported
anchor: a popover is placed against another node's rect from the previous frame
anchor: flip to the other side only when the first side leaves the viewport
relative units and expressions feed real layout without a manager or hidden passes
limitations: The caller identifies the containing block; there is no implicit CSS containing-block search.

items.title: Menus and popovers anchored to geometry
items.research_acceptance: A tooltip near each viewport edge chooses a visible fallback and remains anchored after its target moves.
profiles: Anchors consume explicit/current-or-previous geometry, edge/pivot/offset and viewport fallback data, carrying the subtree with the repositioned root.
verification: anchor: corners and edges of the parent's content box, with the subtree carried along
anchor: no anchors leaves the layout untouched; overflow is reported
anchor: a popover is placed against another node's rect from the previous frame
anchor: flip to the other side only when the first side leaves the viewport
overlay: a window with a menu, a tooltip from last frame's rect and paint layers
limitations: Applications decide when previous-frame geometry is acceptable; layer selection and focus trapping remain explicit.

items.title: Fixed and sticky positioning
items.research_acceptance: A sticky table header remains within its scroll container and stops at its end; nested clipping and input coordinates remain correct.
profiles: Measured fixed/sticky placement accepts explicit containing and scroll boxes, independent start/end constraints and caller chosen stacking. Unconstrained axes retain their measured positions.
verification: both-axis gutters converge, mirror and position thumbs with real offsets
chaining, snap stops, reveal padding and content anchoring combine predictably
limitations: Call between arrangement and finalization; the helper does not observe window/scroll state or create a layer automatically.

items.title: Consistent paint and hit layer order
items.research_acceptance: The visually topmost overlapping eligible widget receives input; global level behavior is not mislabeled nested CSS isolation.
profiles: Global inherited layer order and row order agree between paint and hit queries. Explicit offscreen ranges provide isolated local composition without global translucent reordering.
verification: order: raised nodes and their subtrees paint after layer 0, rows in order within a layer
overlay: a window with a menu, a tooltip from last frame's rect and paint layers
stacking layers: a raised menu paints after every row; batch counts recorded
stacking layers: with no node raised, layer order paints exactly like row order
merge across text: overlapping items keep their order, in row and in layer order
atLayered matches the scalar reference, and is `at` when every layer is 0
atLayered: an open menu covers the later body row under it
expanded targets agree across pure comptime and layered runtime input
ordinary quad text and custom commands participate in an exact clipped isolated group
limitations: Local groups are caller-sequenced surfaces, not a retained CSS stacking-context resolver.

items.title: Visibility, layout and input participation
items.research_acceptance: Hidden-reserved content keeps space; excluded content does not; transparent interactive content follows its explicit hit policy.
profiles: Independent layout/paint/hit/semantic participation combines down the subtree, collapses layout contributions and cancels captured input when a control becomes ineligible.
verification: participation reserves hidden space, collapses layout and cancels descendant input
reuse rebuilds collapsed and cursor-dependent children when their parent changes
recipe participation cancels release actions and explicit cursor wins in both front ends
limitations: Inherited exclusions cannot be re-enabled by a child; choose a separate sibling/subtree for a portal or independently participating overlay.

items.title: Overflow and scrolling semantics
items.research_acceptance: A clip-only container cannot scroll programmatically by accident; automatic bars use the same content extents as input scrolling.
profiles: Native visible/clip geometry remains separate from a measured scroll viewport; both-axis auto/always presentation uses real extents, clipping and input.
verification: clamp: scroll stays between the content start and its end
scroll: a long list scrolled by a wheel, then to a focused row, with a sticky header
two-axis styled viewport consumes input and emits semantic bars through ordinary Frame
both-axis gutters converge, mirror and position thumbs with real offsets
limitations: This is explicit native container behavior, not CSS overflow propagation or anonymous scroll-box construction.

items.title: Containment and virtualized measurement boundaries
items.research_acceptance: Offscreen row styling does not force realization of every row; changing a size-affecting token updates total scroll extent correctly.
profiles: Existing bounded virtualization and relayout boundaries compose with measured placeholders and explicit scroll extent. Reused subtrees rebase sparse paint references and rebuild when inherited participation/cursor inputs change.
verification: reuse: unchanged signals copy the subtree; a changed one rebuilds it once
reuse: a copy moved to other rows has its links rebased
reuse: the pointer over the subtree forces a rebuild
reuse: after the pointer leaves, one more rebuild clears the hover, then reuse resumes
reuse: springs moving outside the subtree do not stop the copy
reuse: a spring moving inside the subtree rebuilds it until it lands, then survives copies
reuse: a copy behind a relayout boundary skips layout and lands where a rebuild would
reuse: no room for the copy means a rebuild, never an overflow
reuse: a copied subtree keeps its extras rows and inherits from its new place
reuse rebuilds collapsed and cursor-dependent children when their parent changes
reuse rebases paint references when an unchanged decorated subtree moves in row storage
virtual list maps a bounded window onto a large data set and clips fractional rows
a conditional root releases its viewport when hidden, then reuses it
check: what a comptime virtual list's state must have
window: the rows on screen by index arithmetic
boundaries: changes inside a boundary leave its natural size, and all outside it, alone
limitations: Visible-range realization and content extents are application inputs. No CSS content-visibility heuristic or asynchronous intrinsic measurement is implied.

items.title: Custom layout through explicit passes
items.research_acceptance: A custom radial layout can use supplied rows and finish through normal paint/input processing with no runtime per-widget callback or hidden allocation.
profiles: Custom measured items/results remain ordinary caller-owned rows; standalone arrange functions produce Placement, Style, Box or text Lines consumed by existing native layout/emission.
verification: special layouts lower into ordinary node layout and preserve dependent placement
table spans and page fragments drive the real placement and glyph-line columns
limitations: No hidden per-widget runtime callbacks or required layout object registry; callers sequence dependent passes.

items.title: Logical geometry and pixel rounding policy
items.research_acceptance: Fractional scaling does not accumulate gaps across a long row, and caret geometry agrees with painted glyph metrics.
profiles: Runtime, plain and folded compile-time layout support fractional or device-grid coordinates and a caller grid origin. Cumulative track/glyph/caret endpoints use the same optional rounding pass.
Explicit none/nearest/floor/ceil policies use device scale and grid origin; cumulative track endpoints avoid drift; the text pass updates glyph, line, justification and caret geometry together.
verification: cumulative rounding preserves shared edges and glyph caret geometry at fractional scale
rounded runtime, plain and folded layouts retain shared fractional geometry
limitations: Fixed-viewport integer compile-time retention rejects fractional policies unless fractional_coordinates is selected. Change the grid from original measurements, not already-snapped text advances.
The text rounding pass runs after placement/bidi and before query/emission, and must restart from raw layout when policy changes.
Stroke alignment is a paint concern; root-owned finalizeWith/runtime integration supplies the corresponding native geometry path.

items.title: Viewport and container style conditions
items.research_acceptance: Resizing one dock panel changes its compact variant without restyling unrelated panels or creating size-query oscillation.
profiles: Explicit viewport/container width and height ranges plus scale ranges select ordinary ordered rules; each request supplies its own container snapshot and optional exact environment cache key.
verification: unknown preferences do not match false; viewport and container conditions stay separate
optional cache agrees with direct resolution and generation changes invalidate a reached state
limitations: Named breakpoint conventions, orientation policy and container measurement scheduling remain caller data/control flow.
There is no retained boundary subscription system or automatic size-query cycle solver.

items.title: Environment and input-capability conditions
items.research_acceptance: Changing a hover capability updates affected recipes only; unknown is distinguishable from an explicit false preference.
profiles: Host data for appearance/accent, text scale, high/forced contrast, reduced effects, pointer precision, hover, direction and unknown preferences drives the same rule evaluation; existing Input/Settings adapters retain unknown-versus-false semantics.
verification: unknown preferences do not match false; viewport and container conditions stay separate
known accessibility inputs consume existing settings and explicit effect choices
default recipe respects environment text scale and keeps focus separate from selected border
locale font preferences and labels lower to real Frame text rows
combined state and environment row participation cancels captured range and radio actions in both front ends
limitations: The resolver does not query an operating system or infer capabilities that the host did not supply.

items.title: Safe-area and viewport occlusion inputs
items.research_acceptance: A focused input and its popup remain within the supplied usable rectangle when a keyboard occlusion region appears.
profiles: Host safe-area/keyboard/occlusion inputs produce an explicit usable rectangle for responsive layout and overlay constraints. Unknown preferences remain distinguishable from false.
verification: unknown preferences do not match false; viewport and container conditions stay separate
known accessibility inputs consume existing settings and explicit effect choices
anchor: flip to the other side only when the first side leaves the viewport
limitations: The framework consumes host measurements; it does not guess display cutouts or keyboard geometry.

items.title: Specialized native and document layouts
items.research_acceptance: An enabled module publishes its supported semantics and capacity limits; disabled modules add no per-node storage requirement.
profiles: Optional bounded dock, radial, flow, masonry, flex, measured spanning table, balanced column height and page/column fragmentation passes produce usable placements/Lines; fragmentation reports relaxed impossible constraints.
verification: special layouts lower into ordinary node layout and preserve dependent placement
bounded flex bases freeze repeatedly and auto margins absorb remaining space
table spans and page fragments drive the real placement and glyph-line columns
limitations: These are measured native/document building blocks, not an HTML formatter or general constraint-equation solver.
Automatic CSS floats, collapsed table-border conflict resolution and footnote placement are not provided by these two modules.

items.title: Advanced text in the normal frame path
items.research_acceptance: An ordinary frame can render and measure a centered wrapped proportional-font label with the same metrics used by hit queries.
profiles: Paragraph rows, rich spans, font-backed metrics, explicit fallback, wrapping, bidi, ellipsis and real transformed glyph emission are consumed by Stack and root's normal Frame.endText path. First/last baseline source is also consumed through the normal Paragraph/Stack path.
verification: paragraph rows drive normal measure wrap query and transformed glyph emission
rich rows preserve shaping and expose per-glyph font size and inherited-opacity paint
golden: a frame measured, wrapped and painted through the stack matches the reference
limitations: The native Stack uses native Shaper values; optional HarfBuzz remains an explicit same-Run producer rather than a mandatory core backend.
Default Frame.end retains the small Mono profile; full text is selected explicitly.

items.title: Family, resource and style matching
items.research_acceptance: A missing requested family chooses the documented fallback; loading a new matching font invalidates dependent metrics without corrupting handles.
profiles: Caller-owned catalog/family lists select actual font handles through CSS-style static width/style/weight ordering; OS/2/head metadata and existing system/embedded fallback adapters remain explicit.
verification: font requests select actual family faces before the ordinary text measure pass
static-face matching respects width priority and the 400 to 500 weight interval
limitations: Family matching is ASCII case-insensitive; platform discovery/canonical Unicode family aliases remain caller-owned.
find returns a catalog index; apply writes catalog[index].font. There is no required global font registry.

items.title: Font weight, width and slant selection
items.research_acceptance: A requested weight selects the correct face when present and follows the stated synthesis fallback when absent.
profiles: Matches real normal/italic/oblique and numeric weight/width faces; optional HarfBuzz synthesis explicitly controls horizontal/vertical emboldening, slant and in-place advance policy with real outline/raster effects.
verification: static-face matching respects width priority and the 400 to 500 weight interval
explicit synthesis changes real outline coverage and matching advances with default reset
limitations: Synthesis is an explicit outline fallback, not an implicit replacement for a real chosen face; SVG/bitmap artwork is not synthesized.
Automatic selection within variable font axis ranges is not part of the static catalog matcher.

items.title: Extended font formats and variable/color fonts
items.research_acceptance: Unsupported formats fail clearly; enabled variable axes alter geometry and metrics with distinct cache keys.
profiles: Optional HB13.2.1 provides TTF/CFF/CFF2/variable outlines, arbitrary explicit variation axes, format diagnostics, COLRv0+CPAL layers, COLRv1 gradients/clips/transforms/groups/compositing, embedded PNG extraction, and plain/gzip OpenType SVG rasterization through actual bounded paint consumers.
verification: variable coordinates change real glyph advances and an empty axis list restores defaults
variable outlines change rasterized coverage through bounded existing path buffers
CFF and CFF2 cubic outlines connect to the same path rasterizer
COLRv0 palettes change real rasterized glyph layer colors
python src/text/shape/testdata/make_variable.py
python src/text/shape/testdata/make_color.py
python src/text/shape/testdata/make_colrv1.py

SVG font support is the renderer's declared bounded SVG profile and returns explicit unsupported-profile errors; it is not full SVG/CSS conformance.
Bitmap extraction supports HarfBuzz's PNG payload route; other embedded codecs are not silently decoded.

items.title: Shaping feature and run-property control
items.research_acceptance: Toggling a supported ligature feature changes the intended run without changing unrelated text; unsupported features are reported by profile.
profiles: Native Paragraph consumes liga/kern/mark flags; optional HB consumes arbitrary OpenType feature tags/values/byte ranges, explicit script/language/direction and cluster-level policy with reset per call.
verification: paint-only spans preserve kerning and ligatures and features remain explicit
explicit feature ranges direction and language reach HarfBuzz and reset per call
limitations: Native Shaper's smaller feature/script profile is retained explicitly; full script shaping uses the optional adapter.
HB shapes one caller-itemized run; callers segment distinct script/language/feature runs before combining outputs.

items.title: Bidi, script and language integration
items.research_acceptance: Arabic mixed with Latin labels and numbers preserves correct visual order and stable logical selection indices.
profiles: Retains Unicode bidi/isolation/script passes and logical/visual caret/selection mapping; paragraph direction is exposed and HB accepts explicit per-run language/script.

Native ligature caret subdivision retains its equal-share policy unless caller metrics supply a finer external caret model.

items.title: Cluster-aware font fallback
items.research_acceptance: A supported joined emoji or base-plus-mark sequence is not broken by per-code-point fallback when one font can render the sequence.
profiles: Fallback chooses a complete Unicode grapheme using nominal font coverage, preserves base+combining/ZWJ/variation sequences in one face and maintains actual face identity through layout/atlas lookup.
verification: cluster fallback moves a base with its mark and never splits an unsupported sequence
Stack fallback keeps a combining sequence in one face through shaping and line layout
limitations: If no face covers the full cluster, the entire cluster stays with a first-scalar/current candidate and unresolved glyphs remain .notdef.
Nominal coverage does not guarantee an emoji ZWJ/variation sequence has a single ligature.
Rich spans have explicit face choices and do not automatically use the plain-paragraph fallback chain.

items.title: Grapheme-safe indexing and editing
items.research_acceptance: Caret movement, backspace and ellipsis never split an extended grapheme cluster, including combined marks and supported emoji sequences.
profiles: Preserves existing UTF-8/grapheme editing and navigation, adds whole-shaped-cluster truncation and read-only behavior across every mutation path.
verification: replayed input: typing, Backspace and Delete by grapheme, Enter
replayed input: the caret moves by grapheme, word and line
start middle and end truncation preserve complete clusters in real glyph output
GraphemeBreakTest.txt
limitations: Display transforms use explicit source maps; applications must use those maps when editing transformed display strings.

items.title: Paragraph alignment and justification
items.research_acceptance: Centered, end-aligned and justified paragraphs use the same measured line widths as painting, including RTL runs.
profiles: Paragraph alignment exposes logical start/end, physical left/right, center, justification and last-line alignment; bidi placement and per-line width overrides use the same line geometry.
verification: paragraph rows drive normal measure wrap query and transformed glyph emission
golden: carets at every offset match the reference
limitations: Justification is advance/space based; language-specific kashida insertion or glyph reshaping is not automatically performed.

items.title: Whitespace, newlines and tabs
items.research_acceptance: Preserved tabs align predictably and copying a visually collapsed label retains the documented original-text behavior.
profiles: Explicit preserve/collapse/preserve-breaks normalization maintains source offsets; paragraph tab size/width and wrapping modes use per-line tab origins and trailing-space handling.
verification: paragraph rows drive normal measure wrap query and transformed glyph emission
intrinsic widths distinguish unbreakable words anywhere tabs and fit content in real layout
limitations: Tab stops are periodic widths, not a mixed per-stop left/right/decimal tab ruler.
Applications decide whether to normalize before a specialized external shaping pass.

items.title: Line-breaking policies and hyphenation
items.research_acceptance: Emergency wrapping preserves clusters; a discretionary hyphen appears only at a chosen break and layout remains bounded.
profiles: UAX14 opportunities, word/keep-all/grapheme policies, emergency breaks, soft hyphens, caller dictionary opportunities and a real Liang Unicode-scalar pattern evaluator feed greedy or bounded quadratic balanced line breaking and visible hyphen marker quads. Explicit Unicode/default, strict, normal, loose and anywhere modes apply bounded Japanese/Chinese punctuation/kana/hyphen/iteration/affix distinctions to actual break opportunities.
verification: patterns create measured hyphen breaks consumed by standard line placement
strict and loose CJK tailoring change real wrapped lines while keeping glue and clusters
limitations: Locale hyphenation patterns/dictionaries and canonical casing are supplied by the caller; no bundled language corpus is claimed.
Tailoring is the declared Unicode16 CJK profile; locale-specific Thai compound-word segmentation and additional publishing traditions require caller opportunities/dictionaries.
Balanced breaking uses constant width and a declared candidate bound; variable leading-line widths use greedy mode and return UnsupportedPolicy for balanced.

items.title: Truncation and maximum visible lines
items.research_acceptance: A middle-truncated path preserves its selected suffix, never splits a cluster and exposes its full value to copying/accessibility.
profiles: Normal paragraphs clamp maximum lines with optional end ellipsis; optional start/middle/end truncation produces real retained glyph rows plus caller-shaped markers and source-range metadata.
verification: paragraph rows drive normal measure wrap query and transformed glyph emission
start middle and end truncation preserve complete clusters in real glyph output
limitations: A fade is composed using paint/mask facilities rather than a separate glyph-breaking mode.
Custom marker callers supply measured/shaped glyphs and matching atlas images.

items.title: Line height, leading and baseline metrics
items.research_acceptance: Mixed font sizes share the selected baseline; larger line spacing avoids glyph/caret clipping and produces matching measured height.
profiles: Paragraph absolute/factor line height and leading distribution use actual font metrics; inline measured boxes supply explicit baselines; document blocks carry before/after spacing; metric-based font-size-adjust changes real text measurement. Font/cap/x-height/em/alphabetic edge helpers trim actual outer line leading while preserving baseline distances; explicit baseline-coordinate rows and shifts update glyph offsets and line metrics together.
verification: paragraph rows drive normal measure wrap query and transformed glyph emission
font requests select actual family faces before the ordinary text measure pass
inline replacement participates in wrapping baseline metrics and transformed image emission
edge trim and selected last baselines drive glyph queries and native baseline layout
span baseline selection changes real offsets and line-height metrics
limitations: Non-alphabetic BASE/MATH coordinate values are explicit caller/shaper inputs; the core helper does not silently guess unavailable font baselines. Trimming is an explicit pass over formatted Lines.
Font-size-adjust's native metric helper uses OS/2 or measured TrueType glyph data; extended HB-only faces can provide their own target metrics.

items.title: Letter and word spacing
items.research_acceptance: Spacing changes update measured width, hit positions and painting consistently without separating required joining behavior.
profiles: Letter and word spacing are consumed once per complete cluster, avoid trailing letter spacing and interact with justification through the shared advances. Font-relative values can be resolved by units.
verification: paragraph rows drive normal measure wrap query and transformed glyph emission
limitations: Negative spacing is clamped to prevent negative cluster advances.
Optional ligatures are disabled for nonzero native letter spacing; full contextual script spacing remains the selected shaper/profile's responsibility.

items.title: Rich text shaping runs versus paint spans
items.research_acceptance: Adding a color-only highlight preserves glyph selection, positions and paragraph width; paint segmentation alone changes.
profiles: Adjacent spans with equal font/size shape together, preserving ligatures/kerning across paint-only boundaries; glyphs retain independent actual font/metric span/color metadata and optional versioned shape-cache reuse.
verification: paint-only spans preserve kerning and ligatures and features remain explicit
rich rows preserve shaping and expose per-glyph font size and inherited-opacity paint
limitations: A glyph crossing paint boundaries takes its cluster-start color; it is not split into clipped multicolor ligature fragments.
Explicit font/size boundaries begin new shaping groups.

items.title: Text decorations
items.research_acceptance: Underline offset and thickness follow resized text; decoration bounds participate in damage and do not alter glyph metrics.
profiles: Real font underline/strike metrics, explicit overrides, underline/overline/strike, solid/double/dotted/dashed/wavy patterns and glyph-ink skipping produce transformed, clipped draw quads. Named/custom emphasis marks shape into real mark images and place per Unicode typographic unit using actual cluster geometry, optional line-height reservation, and upright vertical positions.
verification: decorations consume font metrics patterns ink and transformed selection geometry
emphasis uses ligature shares grapheme exclusions and reserved real line geometry
vertical emphasis remains upright beside actual column geometry
limitations: Skip-ink uses supplied glyph-image ink boxes, not a curve-exact outline subtraction.
Hosts supply an appropriate mark atlas image/font; missing named glyphs return MissingGlyph. Ruby/decorations collisions use explicit gap/placement inputs rather than hidden global typography policy.

items.title: Inline objects and baseline shifts
items.research_acceptance: An inline icon and subscript affect line height correctly and remain selectable/navigable according to the documented index policy.
profiles: Measured U+FFFC replacements alter actual advances/line metrics, place by baseline/text/line alignment and emit image quads; ruby composes measured base/annotation boxes and reserve/overhang policy.
verification: inline replacement participates in wrapping baseline metrics and transformed image emission
ruby reserves measured annotation space and becomes one inline object
limitations: Object measurement/layout is an explicit pass; Stack does not call arbitrary embedded widget callbacks.
Superscript/subscript math composition is owned by the separate optional math module.

items.title: Foreground, background and highlight paint for text
items.research_acceptance: Changing a highlight background or foreground role repaints without changing shaped glyphs; unsupported text paint kinds fail explicitly.
profiles: Authored span foregrounds and selection/background range quads preserve TextRun transform, rounded clipping and inherited opacity without multiplying effective ordinary text color twice.
verification: paragraph quads carry placement, span colour, marker, transform and rounded clipping
rich rows preserve shaping and expose per-glyph font size and inherited-opacity paint
decorations consume font metrics patterns ink and transformed selection geometry
emphasis uses ligature shares grapheme exclusions and reserved real line geometry
limitations: Gradient/stroke text uses the optional outline/path/paint consumers rather than a mandatory style field in every native glyph row.

items.title: Editable text visual parts
items.research_acceptance: A theme swap updates caret/selection/composition appearance without losing composition text, selection endpoints or keyboard focus.
profiles: Real single-line and multiline editors consume content, placeholder, caret, selection foreground/background, support/error and focus recipes while retaining native editor selection/typing/read-only behavior. Selected foreground clips full shaped runs instead of splitting ligatures.

Bar/block/underline carets and arbitrary selection/decoration colors are real geometry consumers; editor retains composition and displayed/source offsets, with read-only blocking mutation and platform input requests.
verification: recipe controls: runtime/comptime draw and behavior parity through click, drag, text and theme changes
forced color selection uses HighlightText in both front ends without duplicate semantics
multiline recipe routes typing, read-only policy and support part to real editor output
caller usage: read-only slider and textfield preserve application values
decorations consume font metrics patterns ink and transformed selection geometry
read-only input preserves selection copy and navigation while rejecting every edit path
replayed input: IME composition shows a preedit range; the commit is one undo step
limitations: The stock single-line profile exposes four native selection bands and nine possible color intervals; distinct selected foreground requires bounded additional clip/text rows.

Specialized IME underline styling, selection handles and richer prefix/suffix/editor decorations can be composed through the separate text decoration/part APIs; the standard recipe does not implement every editor chrome policy.
Blink scheduling, placeholder, prefix/suffix, inactive colors and selection handles are component/host recipe inputs rather than hidden text-editor global policy.

items.title: Locale-aware display text transformations
items.research_acceptance: Locale-sensitive case conversion can change displayed length while selection/copy behavior remains defined against the original text.
profiles: Unicode16 full lower/upper/title/capitalize mappings include expansions, Greek final sigma, Turkish/Azeri/Lithuanian context and Dutch IJ; full-width and grapheme masking preserve explicit display/source offset maps.
verification: display casing expands Unicode and preserves original editing offsets
display masks whole graphemes and orientation distinguishes vertical alternates
limitations: Casing locale selection is the declared root/tr/az/lt/nl profile, not an implicit system locale lookup.
Localized number/date formatting is a separate application service.

items.title: OpenType typographic variants
items.research_acceptance: Tabular digits align changing values without layout jitter when supported; unsupported variants are diagnosed rather than falsely advertised.
profiles: Arbitrary OpenType feature tags and ranges are passed to real HB shaping, covering numeral forms, small caps, fractions, slashed zero, stylistic sets, alternates and localized forms when the selected font supplies them.
verification: explicit feature ranges direction and language reach HarfBuzz and reset per call
limitations: A requested feature cannot create glyphs absent from the font; no synthetic small-caps/figure construction is silently substituted.

items.title: Text cache and invalidation contract
items.research_acceptance: Color-only changes reuse shaped runs; font-feature/language changes invalidate them; width changes yield correct line breaks and caret positions.
profiles: Optional caller-owned native and HB shaping caches carry explicit font identity/reload generation; HB keys include all feature/language/script/direction/cluster/variation/synthesis settings. Native paint-only spans reuse shaping, and existing atlas ownership remains explicit. Embedded PNG strike selection restores prior ppem state, so raster extraction cannot silently alter later shaping/cache behavior.
verification: caller generations prevent reloaded font data from reusing stale cached advances
measure and wrap fill w, h and ascent of the runs in this stack's fonts
optional HarfBuzz cache separates variable instances features language and font generations
glyph images survive eviction and repacking
bitmap color fonts decode with the existing PNG path and SVG extraction is explicit
limitations: No mandatory font-match or paragraph-layout cache is introduced; callers can retain their plain result rows.
Caller resource lifetime/generation discipline is required; omitted native IDs default to local face index and generation zero.
The existing bounded cache uses 63-bit hash identity with the documented collision tradeoff.

items.title: Vertical writing and ruby annotations
items.research_acceptance: Vertical text uses correct glyph orientation and logical edges; ruby contributes documented line extents without disrupting base-text indexing.
profiles: Actual HB vertical advances/substitutions feed bounded RL/LR columns, upright/sideways glyph transforms and UAX50 orientation; explicit measured ruby annotations compose into inline boxes. Upright vertical emphasis marks consume real pens/advances and explicit arranged column boxes.
verification: real vertical advance rows form right-to-left columns and upright or sideways quads
vertical HarfBuzz advances feed the bounded vertical layout consumer
ruby reserves measured annotation space and becomes one inline object
vertical emphasis remains upright beside actual column geometry
limitations: Vertical-alternate availability is an explicit caller/shaper fact; no alternate is fabricated from Unicode orientation alone.
This is measured vertical/ruby composition, not the complete CSS ruby line-breaking and annotation-merging algorithm.
Vertical emphasis space is reserved by caller column width/gap inputs; placing marks does not silently move already-arranged columns.

items.title: Specialist document typography
items.research_acceptance: An optional module declares a bounded supported subset and can be disabled without adding ordinary label storage or work.
profiles: Optional measured mathematical composition and OpenType MATH metrics/variants/assemblies; shaped glyph placement along native polyline tangents; drop-cap width/origin integration; optical edge punctuation; bounded UTF-8 counter systems/scopes and baseline-aligned list markers. All use native glyph/rule/quad consumers without ordinary label storage.
verification: fraction enters inline layout and positions real paragraph quads plus rule
scripts limits radicals and matrices reserve actual measured extents
OpenType MATH constants and extender assembly become glyph quads with bounded storage
shaped line follows native path tangents and retains transform opacity clipping
drop cap changes real line breaks positions and caret coordinates in both directions
hanging edge punctuation moves glyphs and carets together without splitting clusters
counter systems format UTF8 exact integers and reject invalid and insufficient storage
nested scoped counters reset increment and format without mutating ancestors

limitations: No TeX/MathML parser or formula AST; callers shape leaves, choose script sizes and supply measured boxes. MATH device hint corrections are not evaluated.
Text-on-path caret/hit projection remains caller work; path rendering retains source clusters and transforms.
Drop-cap variable leading widths use the greedy breaker; balanced breaking returns UnsupportedPolicy. Hanging punctuation preserves existing breaks rather than reoptimizing justified paragraphs.
Counter algorithms have declared native conventions rather than complete CSS Counters/CLDR conformance. Footnotes/pagination belong to separate document-layout modules.

items.title: Pointer cursor appearance
items.research_acceptance: Overlapping widgets select the topmost eligible cursor; custom hotspots are scaled consistently and unsupported cursors use an explicit fallback.
profiles: 35 cursor values with inheritance/default reset, platform mappings and declared fallback fidelity. Custom images use an ordinary texture quad with explicit hotspot, hardware hiding and old/new damage.
verification: setCursor: the last request that holds wins; the next frame starts at arrow
style cursor inherits through paint extras and explicit arrow overrides it
custom cursor uploads through ordinary image draw, respects hotspot and damages movement
x11: the cursor the frame asks for is the one the server shows
limitations: Windows/macOS methods were cross-compiled; actual native sessions were unavailable. Wayland protocol/fallback fixtures and Web syntax were checked.
The caller owns custom-image upload and final quad emission; platform-specific unavailable cursor shapes use documented fallbacks.

items.title: Visual and hit-target geometry policy
items.research_acceptance: A visually transformed button receives clicks where it is painted; expanded neighboring targets resolve overlap deterministically.
profiles: Caller-owned sorted hit-policy entries add local padding/minimum dimensions and rectangle/rounded/ellipse/path shapes. The chosen hit drives the ordinary capture/release path; runtime and pure compile-time use common inverse-transform and ancestor-clip geometry. Simultaneous contacts use caller-computed rows through Touches.stepWithHits while retaining capture by platform contact ID.
verification: expanded transformed targets preserve clipping, ordering, real activation and unchanged paint
path targets share evenodd/nonzero holes and validate ambiguous expansion
expanded targets agree across pure comptime and layered runtime input
pure comptime affine painting and exact hit agree with the runtime tree
Touches: enlarged caller targets preserve capture across reordered contacts and reject count changes atomically
Touches: removed hidden or nonsensing owners cancel before missing-contact release and cannot reactivate mid-press
shared choice slots paint and hit only the active hosted region
unshared inactive choice targets stay absent while ordinary offscreen targets can expand
limitations: Path expansion is deliberately rejected; callers must provide a dilated path when needed. Empty/collapsed rows are never revived.
Pure compile-time target enumeration uses descriptor order; runtime accepts explicit layer rows.

items.title: Keyboard-visible focus styling policy
items.research_acceptance: Keyboard navigation produces a visible focus indicator without changing layout; hover/selected states cannot erase it unintentionally.
profiles: Actual input modality and always-show-focus select an independent focus part; the native outside outline references current border-box geometry without layout or hit participation. Selection/hover styling does not replace the ring.
verification: default recipe respects environment text scale and keeps focus separate from selected border
recipe disabled state cancels capture, skips Tab and cannot be defeated by a visual override
radio and range recipes preserve keyboard and pointer behavior with shared marks and two visible thumbs
native outline can satisfy AA focus visibility while failing the separate AAA area diagnostic
limitations: Focus-within and focus-scroll policy are explicit owner/runtime inputs; no semantic relationship is inferred from decorative part names.
Visibility, adjacent contrast and AAA changed-pixel area are separate diagnostics rather than a compliance certification.

items.title: Behavioral state and visual-state consistency
items.research_acceptance: A disabled control is non-activating regardless of its colors, and read-only text can preserve allowed selection/copy behavior.
profiles: Authoritative disabled/read-only state gates real behavior in both front ends, cancels stale capture and preserves allowed read-only navigation. Invalid/required/busy use reserved u16 semantic bits with existing ordinals intact, survive Export/diff and reach AccessKit properties.
Mode.read_only retains navigation, selection and copy while rejecting typing, deletion, cut/paste, undo/redo mutation and IME commit; it cancels preedit and avoids keyboard input requests.
verification: recipe disabled state cancels capture, skips Tab and cannot be defeated by a visual override
recipe read-only checkbox remains focusable and its pointer event is explicitly suppressed
caller usage: read-only slider and textfield preserve application values
extra recipe controls cancel disabled capture and keep read-only groups focusable without changes
tree export: validation requirement and busy state retain the existing compact state ABI
diagnostics compare recipe state with actual exported semantics including validation and busy
accesskit: a text input's text goes out as its value, its placeholder as placeholder
read-only input preserves selection copy and navigation while rejecting every edit path
limitations: Busy, invalid and required are distinct from disabled; applications choose their validation/action policy.
The inspected Web shell has no DOM semantic-tree or JSON state serializer; host Web accessibility integration is not claimed.
Native AccessKit execution is a separate optional build gate and must be read with the validation record.
Other component states are handled by root/theme recipe consumers; this row covers the authoritative editor behavior only.

items.title: High contrast and system color palettes
items.research_acceptance: Switching high contrast preserves legible text and identifiable control boundaries in both light and dark profiles.

system colors override authored paint with provenance and explicit component exceptions

limitations: The resolver consumes host color data and does not itself query native system palettes.
Arbitrary host palettes, images, filters and translucent backdrops require actual samples; no universal contrast guarantee is inferred from a semantic role name.

items.title: User text scale and spacing tolerance
items.research_acceptance: Large text and user spacing settings do not clip labels, hide values or make primary controls unreachable.
profiles: Explicit text scaling updates semantic type tokens and actual text metrics; paragraph line/letter/word spacing overrides reach Stack layout; fit-sized controls expand for longer localized labels.
Text size, metric-based size adjustment, line/word/letter spacing and actual intrinsic/wrapped remeasurement are exposed to caller theme/text-scale policy.
verification: default recipe respects environment text scale and keeps focus separate from selected border

locale font preferences and labels lower to real Frame text rows
font requests select actual family faces before the ordinary text measure pass
paragraph rows drive normal measure wrap query and transformed glyph emission
intrinsic widths distinguish unbreakable words anywhere tabs and fit content in real layout
limitations: Environment textFactor clamps the convenience scale to 0.5..4; direct typed sizes remain available.
Applications still choose wrapping, scroll/reflow, maximum dimensions and minimum hit policies; no automatic claim is made that every fixed-size custom layout remains usable at every text setting.
The toolkit does not guarantee every application avoids clipping; hosts must remeasure after user scale/spacing changes and choose content-preserving constraints.

items.research_acceptance: Preference changes replace translucent surfaces with readable opaque equivalents and preserve already-supported reduced-motion behavior.

recipe spinner wake follows effective ancestor participation and the bound busy state in both front ends
limitations: Essential animation is an explicit caller decision; arbitrary custom effects and scroll policy must consume the same preferences through their own native interfaces.
Decorative surface opacity policy does not forcibly alter content/group alpha that may carry application meaning.

items.research_acceptance: Error, checked and selected states remain distinguishable in a grayscale/system-color rendering and agree with accessibility state.

radio and range recipes preserve keyboard and pointer behavior with shared marks and two visible thumbs

items.research_acceptance: A themed scrollbar supports distinct hover/drag states and never paints a thumb below the configured minimum length.

verification: two-axis styled viewport consumes input and emits semantic bars through ordinary Frame

items.research_acceptance: Nested scroll containers follow an explicit chaining policy; snap targets remain reachable and reduced-motion preferences are respected.

items.research_acceptance: Tabbing to an offscreen input reveals it through nested scrollers without unexpectedly jumping unrelated containers.

items.title: Everyday control part recipes
items.research_acceptance: A shared theme can style all listed controls and their disabled/focused/selected states without copying widget implementations.
profiles: Dedicated shared-recipe adapters cover button/icon/label, checkbox/radio marks, switch, slider/two-thumb range, progress, spinner, single-line input and multiline editor/support parts. Radio/range reuse existing pure key/pointer behavior; spinner scheduling honors reduced motion. Composite failures preserve inert descriptor rows for later siblings and recover on the next valid frame; row participation is checked before actions; spinner wakes follow the completed subtree and bound busy state.
verification: caller usage: custom icon/label retains button activation and disabled prevents it
recipe controls: runtime/comptime draw and behavior parity through click, drag, text and theme changes
radio and range recipes preserve keyboard and pointer behavior with shared marks and two visible thumbs
extra recipe controls cancel disabled capture and keep read-only groups focusable without changes
recipe spinner requests frames while busy and has a stable reduced-motion alternative in both front ends

Value bubbles, arbitrary tick collections and application-specific input prefix/suffix composition use explicit additional parts; they are not synthesized by the standard controls.

items.title: Navigation and overlay part recipes
items.research_acceptance: A theme change updates every popup/navigation part while preserving accelerator alignment, overflow behavior and focus navigation.
profiles: Dedicated runtime menu, popover, tooltip, breadcrumb and toast compositions resolve plain recipe values into actual Frame rows and Texts while reusing native pure behavior. Compile-time Menu/Popover/Tooltip/Toast hooks reuse ComptimePage, and breadcrumb reuses ComptimeUi focus handling. Dynamic token/recipe/environment and optional menu content spans are caller-owned. Accelerator and indicator strings use named styled parts, separators emit actual noninteractive geometry and are skipped by menu navigation. Tooltip arrows are optional transformed-shape rows with independently resolved paint/geometry. Popover Part.text/Part.content optionally override label typography/bytes, preserving bound labels when null. Label bytes are borrowed until the existing bounded Strings copy; CT recipe content preflights remaining string capacity and reports NoSpace without overwriting. Recipe failures occur before runtime menu action commit; CT hook failure_field retains the first error until the next step. Hidden/collapsed popup panels remove their scrims, while read-only focused controls retain tooltips.

Dedicated shared-recipe menu/popover/tooltip/breadcrumb/toast compositions, plus navigation rows and tabs, reuse existing caller-owned state and pure behavior.
